si_contract.pressure: pGaugePa is actual gauge pressure at each physical cylinder group; kgf/cm² -> Pa uses98066.5 exactly. Do not convert by100000 or treat gauge as absolute.
si_contract.interpretation: Actual pressing is normal force on a shoe. Calculated/equivalent pressing Kr is a separate reduction for operational braking calculations. Shoe count multiplies force AFTER evaluating mu on one shoe.
si_contract.calculated_only: GOST composite Kr_kN=1.22*Kd_kN*(.1*Kd+20)/(.4*Kd+20), paired with phiCalculated=.36*(v+150)/(2v+150). Do not use Kr with actual mu, or actual total with calculated mu.
si_contract.gost_pressure_history: Do not layer GOST equation13 normative20s pressing curve on measured native pressure history; use real pneumatics once.
si_contract.motion_owner: Capacity is nonnegative; LTD owns signed opposition, zero-speed holding/stiction and wheel/rail adhesion. Four bogie pressures are evaluated separately before summing.

friction_models.units: K is actual per-shoe normal force in kN; v is speed magnitude in km/h; coefficients are dimensionless empirical reference laws.
friction_models.standard_cast_iron: .60*(1.6*K+100)/(8*K+100)*(v+100)/(5*v+100) [rounded SI form of PTR generic law]
friction_models.phosphorus_cast_iron: .50*(1.6*K+100)/(5.2*K+100)*(v+100)/(5*v+100) [PTR phosphorus law; same coefficients also given by Galai2017(1) for genericM]
friction_models.old_tf_comparison: A legacy tf argument N/9806.65 with1/4 composite factors differs from the modern .1/.4-kN argument by1.97162% in argument scale, not a tenfold error. The old P10 24/80 and150/5v+150 coefficients have no support in the checked PTR text.
limits: Dry/reference empirical shoe-wheel friction, no explicit temperature, moisture, ice, wear or manufacturing-variation state.
No source proves exact current2ЭС6 flanged-shoe formulation. Generic cast iron is an explicit surrogate.
The Galai paper warns flanged0.0476m² and standard0.0305m² areas differ; a material/geometry-specific fit is a future calibration.

published_numeric_checks.gost_G9_max_limit: Published9.48/21.58kN are not expectations for the fixed effectiveness profile: that profile gives8.66387/20.76412kN at160/340kPa. Values9.48/21.58 are reproduced by minstrokeF1=940.5N and F2=0; this is an observed numerical reconciliation, not proof of missing normative assumptions.

native_comparison.oracle: outputs/TrainerNativeBrakeForceProvider.cs:107; POEZD internal1DBC; oracle-contract.json documents raw body/relocations.
native_comparison.wagon_constants: A994cm²,lever5.79,*.00085,Psend nativekgf/cm²; FTk0 composite branch; output unit10kN.
findings: The publication explicitly requires per-shoe K and separate shoe count. Native wagon K=A*Psend*lever*.00085 instead represents aggregate tf-like pressing; feeding the aggregate to nonlinear mu is not equivalent to summing eight per-shoe forces.

Legacy.00085 can be reconstructed as.85/1000 with area in cm² and pressure in kgf/cm², giving tf-like aggregate pressing. Native output uses10kN/tf-like unit, not the SI9806.65N/tf. These are identified approximations, not proof of current OEM efficiency.
Do not rescale a scientific per-shoe force to reproduce the old oracle. Keep the oracle as diagnostic comparison only.

Current locomotive candidate per-pad correction uses4.4per shoe,4cyl/8pads perbogie but retains legacy.00085, approximate10kN scale and roundedM-like friction. New reference uses explicit SI cylinder/rigging losses and1200N spring.
native_comparison.unit_reconciliation: With k=Kshoe_kN/10, native composite factors are .055*(k+20)/(k+5)*(vms+41.7)/(vms+20.85), approximately the GOST SI per-shoe law. Native castiron factors are .031*(k+6.25)/(k+1.92)*(vms+27.78)/(vms+5.56), approximately the published M/phosphorus law (.03076923,1.9230769 exact converted values). This identifies a rounded tf-like argument scale, not a10x K-unit defect.
